angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 184,361 km at 6.86 pc = 0.36 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 145.6922 +/- 0.0244 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 6.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.265 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Winters et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LTT 1445 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..168W/abstract): 184,361 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.257 +/- 0.014 solar masses from Winters et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LTT 1445 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..168W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3340 +/- 150 K from Winters et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LTT 1445 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..168W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Winters et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LTT 1445 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..168W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ltt-1445-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.002, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 1445 A (pscomppars): spectral type M3.0, from Oddo et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, BD-17 588A: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 1445 A (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.34 dex, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 1445 A (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.04591, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/AJ/168/234/table10 (Flares & flaring stars from TESS & machine learning), column Prot: 1.39717 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 5 catalogued periods, 4 of them within 20% of it

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 1445 A (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3.4 km/s, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.265 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.354. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curves of sectors 4 and 31 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138): 1.41 d, the light swinging by 1.1% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
